> **What you can defend when you leave.** Close the cycle as its director: run the final review under your own rules, decide whether the work is ready to leave your hands, and turn the largest unresolved limitation into the next study.

## The milestone ahead {#checkpoint}

The book opened with one rule: AI is your arm, not your brain. This studio is where the rule graduates. In the final review your tool count may be zero, one, or many — a single assistant, or a directed team of writer, skeptic, and auditor that the two agent lessons show you how to wire and when to overrule — and the release standard does not change with the count. Every public claim must sit inside its evidence and permissions, and the package must still match the cold run that tested it; the agent lessons add records when you used several loops, never a substitute for the audit. What no tool can do is make the two decisions this milestone exists for: whether this work is ready to leave your hands, and what should be asked next. The book closes where it began: tools extend your reach, and the decision about what leaves your hands remains yours.

This studio closes with **[Milestone 12: Your release and next cycle](milestone12-release-next-cycle.qmd)**, a short chapter of its own after the lessons. **What it asks you to produce.** A release audit recording release or withhold-pending-a-named-repair, your final dossier with a complete manifest, an explicit stopping rule, and your next-study agenda.

This is where the chain closes, on a decision. If the audit clears, the artifact leaves your hands; if it does not, this version names the repair that still blocks release. Either way the next-study agenda opens the cycle that follows. The milestone chapter keeps the working details: the practice steps, the versioned record, and how the artifact is assessed.

## The lessons in this studio

Read them in order, working each lesson's **It is your turn** as you go. Each one builds a piece of Milestone 12; beside each lesson is the piece it hands you.

- [Lesson 37 — Managing Multiple AI Agents](https://davi-moreira.github.io/2026F_evidence_driven_research_purdue_HONR464/book/part6-after-conference/35-managing-multiple-ai-agents.html): if you ran several agent loops in your final review: their scoped jobs, the wiring and turn counts, and the one node you kept human.
- [Lesson 38 — Conflicting Agents and Human Escalation](https://davi-moreira.github.io/2026F_evidence_driven_research_purdue_HONR464/book/part6-after-conference/36-conflicting-agents-and-human-escalation.html): if several roles returned a load-bearing verdict: your escalation rules, and one agreement or disagreement diagnosed and settled by your own check, with any override on record.
- [Lesson 39 — Final Research and AI-Management Portfolio](https://davi-moreira.github.io/2026F_evidence_driven_research_purdue_HONR464/book/part6-after-conference/37-final-research-and-ai-management-portfolio.html): your finished research artifact with every claim bounded, your AI-management portfolio in the form your review mode produced, and the rehearsed three-movement defense.

When the last lesson closes, the milestone chapter is next. Nothing you write in a lesson is busywork: every piece above is on the milestone's checklist.
